domain: Contractors State License Law (B&P Code Division 3, Chapter 9), Articles 1-4: administration provisions that touch contractors, application of chapter (definitions of contractor, advertising rules, unlicensed-contracting crimes and citations, required contract notices, license numbers, joint ventures, vehicle signage, license proof in lawsuits, permits), exemptions (B&P 7040-7054.5, incl. owner-builder 7044 and minor work 7048) and classifications (7055-7057)
source_doc: 2026 CSLB California Contractors License Law & Reference Book (official), Section VI, PDF pages 215-271 (Chapter 9 table of contents, then B&P Code sections 7000 through 7057); file chunk lawbook_p216-270.txt

rules.title: City/county may require business tax proof before permit
rules.plain_english: A city or county can make you prove you are current on its local business tax before it issues a building permit, and can deny the permit if you are not. The local business tax itself cannot exceed the license tax/fee allowed by Gov Code 37101 or B&P 16000.

parameters.who_may_require: city, county, or city and county
parameters.trigger: before issuance of any city/county permit
parameters.consequence: permit may be denied to licensed contractor not in compliance

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors applying for local building permits
rules.verbatim_quote: Nothing in this code shall be interpreted to prohibit cities, counties, and cities and counties from denying the issuance of a permit to a licensed contractor who is not in compliance with local business tax requirements.
rules.notes: Permissive for local governments; check each jurisdiction's permit checklist for a business tax certificate.

rules.title: No CSLB civil penalty if Labor Commissioner already penalized same offense
rules.plain_english: If the Labor Commissioner already assessed a civil penalty against you under Labor Code 1020 or 1022 for an offense, CSLB's registrar cannot also assess a civil penalty for that same offense.

parameters.bar_applies_when: Labor Commissioner assessed civil penalty under Labor Code 1020 or 1022

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors penalized by the Labor Commissioner
rules.verbatim_quote: The registrar shall not assess a civil penalty against a licensed contractor who has been assessed a specified civil penalty by the Labor Commissioner under Section 1020 or 1022 of the Labor Code for the same offense.
rules.notes: Labor Code 1020/1022 are not reproduced in this chunk. Bars only the civil penalty; other CSLB discipline is not addressed here.

rules.title: CSLB enforcement: unlicensed activity, workers' comp, jobsite access
rules.plain_english: CSLB has a separate enforcement division that goes after unlicensed activity and contractors without valid workers' compensation coverage. Its special investigators can write you a notice to appear in court, and when working with the Joint Enforcement Strike Force they have free access to all places of labor (job sites).

enforces: obligation to secure valid and current workers' compensation insurance (Labor Code 3700.5)
special_investigator_powers: issue written notice to appear in court (Penal Code 853.5 et seq.)
parameters.jobsite_access: free access to all places of labor when participating in Joint Enforcement Strike Force on the Underground Economy (UI Code 329)

rules.applies_to: All contractors and job sites in California
rules.verbatim_quote: When participating in the activities of the Joint Enforcement Strike Force on the Underground Economy pursuant to Section 329 of the Unemployment Insurance Code, the enforcement division shall have free access to all places of labor.
rules.notes: Separately, B&P 7011.5 gives designated Special Investigations Unit investigators peace-officer authority while investigating CSLB laws (PDF pages 230-231).

rules.title: Filing a knowingly false complaint against a licensee
rules.plain_english: If you are subject to CSLB licensure and you file or cause a complaint against another licensee that you know is false, CSLB can cite you and may refer you to the district attorney or city attorney.

parameters.who: any person subject to licensure under the chapter
parameters.conduct: reporting or causing complaint of professional misconduct against a licensee, knowing it to be false
sanctions: notification to district attorney or city attorney

rules.applies_to: Contractors and other persons subject to CSLB licensure
rules.verbatim_quote: Any person subject to licensure under this chapter who reports to, or causes a complaint to be filed with, the Contractors State License Board that a person licensed by that entity has engaged in professional misconduct, knowing the report or complaint to be false, may be issued a citation by the registrar.
rules.notes: Penalty amount not stated in this section.

rules.title: Definitions: personnel of record, person, qualifier
rules.plain_english: Personnel of record are everyone CSLB's records list as associated with a license. A 'person' includes individuals and every kind of business entity, including federally recognized tribes. A qualifier (qualifying person/individual) is the person who qualifies the license under B&P 7068.

parameters.personnel_of_record: every person listed in the registrar's records as then associated with a licensee

rules.applies_to: All licensees and applicants
rules.verbatim_quote: “Members of the personnel of record” as used in this chapter means every person listed in the records of the registrar as then associated with a licensee.
rules.notes: Personnel of record matter for B&P 7028.5 (cannot contract individually without own license).

rules.title: Federally recognized tribes can be licensed
rules.plain_english: CSLB must license a federally recognized California tribe (or a tribe-controlled entity) that applies under B&P 7065 and otherwise complies. Licensure does not give CSLB authority to regulate activity within a participating tribe's own jurisdiction.

parameters.eligible: federally recognized tribe located in California on the Federal Register list (25 U.S.C. 5131), including an entity controlled by and established for one or more tribes

rules.applies_to: Tribes and tribal entities doing contracting work; owners hiring tribal contractors
rules.verbatim_quote: The board shall license a federally recognized tribe that applies for licensure under Section 7065 and is otherwise compliant with the provisions of this chapter for the purpose of engaging in a business regulated by this chapter.
rules.notes: Related exemption: B&P 7040 exempts tribes acting within tribal jurisdiction in official capacity.

rules.title: Who is a 'contractor' (license trigger)
rules.plain_english: Anyone who builds, alters, repairs, adds to, improves, moves, wrecks or demolishes any building, road, excavation or other structure or improvement, or any part of it, needs a license. This includes offering to do the work, claiming you can, bidding on it, or doing it through others. Subcontractors, specialty contractors, scaffolding, related site cleanup, roadway traffic control and underground storage tank monitoring equipment work are covered.

license_triggers: purports to have capacity to undertake
does work personally or by or through others
subjects: other structure, project, development or improvement
also_covered: erection of scaffolding or other structures or works in connection therewith
cleaning of grounds or structures in connection therewith
preparation and removal of roadway construction zones, lane closures, flagging, or traffic diversions
installation, repair, maintenance, or calibration of underground storage tank monitoring equipment
parameters.roadway_includes: public or city streets, highways, or any public conveyance

rules.applies_to: Anyone performing or offering construction work in California
rules.verbatim_quote: a contractor is any person who undertakes to or offers to undertake to, or purports to have the capacity to undertake to, or submits a bid to, or does himself or herself or by or through others, construct, alter, repair, add to, subtract from, improve, move, wreck or demolish any building, highway, road, parking facility, railroad, excavation or other structure, project, development or improvement
rules.notes: Covered whether or not the work involves adding materials or merchandise. Exemptions are in B&P 7040-7054.5.

rules.title: Servicing fixed HVAC/refrigeration requires license
rules.plain_english: Maintaining or servicing air-conditioning, heating or refrigeration equipment that is a fixed part of a structure is contracting work that requires a license, unless you are an exempt employee under B&P 7053.

parameters.condition: equipment is a fixed part of the structure to which it is attached

rules.applies_to: HVAC/refrigeration service companies
rules.verbatim_quote: Any person not exempt under Section 7053 who maintains or services air-conditioning, heating, or refrigeration equipment that is a fixed part of the structure to which it is attached.
rules.notes: Specific classification (e.g., C-20) is not named in this section.

rules.title: Construction consultants to owner-builders need a license
rules.plain_english: A consultant who helps an owner-builder on a home improvement project by providing or overseeing bids, or by scheduling and overseeing contractors and subs, is a contractor and must be licensed.

consultant_criteria_any_of: provides or oversees a bid for a construction project
arranges for and sets up work schedules for contractors and subcontractors and maintains oversight of a construction project
parameters.context: work under a home improvement contract (B&P 7151.2)
not_a_consultant: owner of the privately owned real property to be improved

rules.applies_to: Construction managers/consultants working for owner-builders on home improvement projects
rules.verbatim_quote: Any person, consultant to an owner-builder, firm, association, organization, partnership, business trust, corporation, or company, who or which undertakes, offers to undertake, purports to have the capacity to undertake, or submits a bid to construct any building or home improvement project, or part thereof.
rules.notes: A tool can flag 'owner's rep' or 'construction consultant' roles on residential projects as requiring a CSLB license.

rules.title: Temporary labor agencies supplying construction workers
rules.plain_english: A temp labor agency that is the employer of workers it supplies for licensed construction work counts as a contractor, unless a properly licensed contractor supervises the work under B&P 7068.1 and is directly responsible for the final results. The qualifier does not have to be present during supervision.

parameters.is_contractor_when: temp labor service agency, as employer, provides employees for work covered by the chapter
parameters.exception: a properly licensed contractor exercises supervision per B&P 7068.1 and is directly responsible for the final results

rules.applies_to: Staffing agencies and contractors using temporary labor
rules.verbatim_quote: A temporary labor service agency that, as the employer, provides employees for the performance of work covered by this chapter. The provisions of this paragraph shall not apply if there is a properly licensed contractor who exercises supervision in accordance with Section 7068.1 and who is directly responsible for the final results of the work.
rules.notes: See companion rule provide-license-number-to-temp-agency.

rules.title: Give your license number to the temp labor agency
rules.plain_english: When you request workers from a temporary labor service agency, you must give the agency your contractor's license number.

parameters.trigger: contractor requests services of a temporary labor service agency

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors using temporary labor service agencies
rules.verbatim_quote: A contractor requesting the services of a temporary labor service agency shall provide his or her license number to that temporary labor service agency.
rules.notes: Can be generated automatically on staffing requests/purchase orders.

rules.title: Tree removal, pruning, stump removal, cabling need license
rules.plain_english: Tree removal, tree pruning, stump removal and tree or limb cabling/guying are contracting work. Exceptions: a nurseryperson's incidental pruning or guying of planted trees, and a gardener's incidental pruning of trees under 15 feet tall after planting.

covered_activities: tree or limb cabling or guying
parameters.gardener_exception_condition: incidental pruning in normal course of routine work; tree must measure less than 15 feet in height after planting
parameters.nurseryperson_exception: incidental pruning of trees, or guying of planted trees and their limbs, in normal course of routine work

rules.applies_to: Tree service companies, gardeners, nurseries
rules.verbatim_quote: Any person not otherwise exempt by this chapter, who performs tree removal, tree pruning, stump removal, or engages in tree or limb cabling or guying. ... The term contractor does not include a gardener who in the normal course of routine work performs incidental pruning of trees measuring less than 15 feet in height after planting.
rules.notes: The minor-work exemption (B&P 7048, under $1,000) may still apply separately if all of its conditions are met.

verification.note: Gardener exception is strictly "less than 15 feet in height after planting"; last amended Stats 2013 ch 319, effective Jan 1, 2014.

rules.title: Water, cathodic protection and monitoring wells need license
rules.plain_english: Drilling, digging, boring, constructing, deepening, repairing, reperforating or abandoning a water well, cathodic protection well or monitoring well is contracting work requiring a license. The agricultural exemption in B&P 7049 does not cover water wells.
rules.applies_to: Well drillers; general contractors and owners with well work in scope
rules.source_location: 2026 CSLB Law Book, PDF pages 239 and 268
rules.verbatim_quote: Any person engaged in the business of drilling, digging, boring, or otherwise constructing, deepening, repairing, reperforating, or abandoning any water well, cathodic protection well, or monitoring well.
rules.notes: B&P 7057(c) bars a B general building contractor from contracting for C-57 well drilling unless it holds the classification or subcontracts it.

rules.title: HOA/common interest development managers excluded
rules.plain_english: A common interest development (HOA) manager performing management services does not need a contractor's license and is not a 'contractor' or 'consultant' under the law.

parameters.scope_of_exclusion: management services as defined in B&P 11500(d)

rules.applies_to: HOA/CID managers and the associations they manage
rules.verbatim_quote: The term “contractor” or “consultant” does not include a common interest development manager, as defined in Section 11501, and a common interest development manager is not required to have a contractor’s license when performing management services, as defined in subdivision (d) of Section 11500.
rules.notes: Exclusion is limited to management services; actual construction work still requires licensed contractors.

rules.title: Mobilehome installation/repair on site is contracting
rules.plain_english: Installing, altering, repairing or preparing to move a mobilehome or mobilehome accessory building on a site for use as a dwelling requires a license. The manufacturer is excluded for off-site construction and warranty-only work; onsite work beyond warranty requires a license.

manufacturer_excluded_when: constructed at a place other than the installation site
manufacturer_included_when: onsite construction, alteration, or repair per specialized plans, specifications, or models
any work other than warranty compliance

rules.applies_to: Mobilehome installers, manufacturers, dealers
rules.verbatim_quote: For the purposes of this chapter, “contractor” includes any person engaged in the business of the construction, installation, alteration, repair, or preparation for moving of a mobilehome or mobilehome accessory buildings and structures upon a site for the purpose of occupancy as a dwelling.
rules.notes: Mobilehomes are not 'personal property' (B&P 7046) or 'finished products' (B&P 7045) for exemption purposes.

rules.title: Mobilehome dealer: written installer certification to buyer
rules.plain_english: A licensed manufactured home/mobilehome dealer does not need a contractor's license if a licensed contractor does the installation and the dealer certifies this in writing to the buyer before installation, giving the installer's name, business address and license number.

parameters.who: seller holding retail manufactured home or mobilehome dealer's license (HSC 18045 et seq.)
parameters.condition: installation performed by a licensed contractor
parameters.timing: prior to performance of the installation

rules.applies_to: Manufactured home and mobilehome dealers and their buyers
rules.verbatim_quote: The certification shall include the name, business address, and contractor’s license number of the licensed contractor by whom the installation will be performed.
rules.notes: Without the timely written certification the dealer does not get the exclusion.

rules.title: Carpet installation: license or written dealer certification
rules.plain_english: Installing carpet attached to the structure by conventional methods requires a license. A retail furniture dealer selling installed carpet is exempt only if a licensed contractor installs it and the dealer certifies this in writing to the buyer before installation, with the installer's name, business address and license number.

parameters.covered: installs or contracts for installation of carpet attached to the structure by any conventional method
parameters.dealer_exemption_holder: retail furniture dealer licensed under B&P 19000 et seq.
parameters.condition: installation performed by a licensed contractor
parameters.timing: prior to performance of the installation

rules.applies_to: Flooring installers and carpet retailers
rules.verbatim_quote: a seller of installed carpet who holds a retail furniture dealer’s license under Chapter 3 (commencing with Section 19000) of Division 8 shall not be required to have a contractor’s license if the installation of the carpet is performed by a licensed contractor and the seller so certifies in writing to the buyer prior to the performance of the installation
rules.notes: Installed carpets are not 'finished products' under the B&P 7045 exemption.

rules.title: C-47 General Manufactured Housing scope
rules.plain_english: The C-47 General Manufactured Housing classification covers manufactured homes, mobilehomes and multifamily manufactured homes.
rules.applies_to: C-47 licensees; owners hiring for manufactured housing
rules.verbatim_quote: the permissible scope of work for the General Manufactured Housing Contractor (C-47) license classification set forth in Section 832.47 of Division 8 of Title 16 of the California Code of Regulations shall include manufactured homes, as defined in Section 18007 of the Health and Safety Code, mobilehomes

rules.title: Who may install fire protection systems
rules.plain_english: Fire protection systems (other than electrical alarm systems) may be installed only by a contractor holding the fire protection classification, or by an owner-builder of an owner-occupied single-family home if no more than two homes on the same parcel are built within one year and the local building department approves the plans and inspects and approves the installation.

allowed_installers: contractor holding fire protection contractor classification (per board regulations)
owner-builder of owner-occupied single-family dwelling meeting conditions

rules.applies_to: Fire sprinkler/fire protection installers; general contractors; owner-builders
rules.verbatim_quote: Except as provided in Section 7026.13, the installation of a fire protection system, excluding an electrical alarm system, shall be performed only by either of the following: (a) A contractor holding a fire protection contractor classification, as defined in the regulations of the board.
rules.notes: The classification code (commonly C-16) is not named in this text; it is defined in board regulations. B&P 7026.13, referenced here, was repealed in 2017. See also B&P 7057(c).

rules.title: Advertising as a contractor brings you under the law
rules.plain_english: If you advertise, put out signs or cards, or list yourself in a directory under a construction category so the public would think you are a contractor, the Contractors License Law applies to you even if your work would otherwise be exempt.

triggers: advertising indicating to the public that the person is a contractor
name or business name in a classified advertisement or directory under a construction or work-of-improvement classification

rules.applies_to: Anyone marketing construction services
rules.verbatim_quote: Any person who advertises or puts out any sign or card or other device that would indicate to the public that he or she is a contractor ... is subject to the provisions of this chapter regardless of whether his or her operations as a builder are otherwise exempted.
rules.notes: Compare B&P 7027.2 (narrow permission for unlicensed advertising under $1,000 with a not-licensed statement).

rules.title: Advertise only in classifications you hold
rules.plain_english: It is a misdemeanor to advertise construction work unless you hold a valid license in the classification advertised. A licensed A (general engineering) or B (general building) contractor may advertise as a 'general contractor'. 'Advertise' includes cards, signs, building markings, print, broadcast, electronic/online and directory listings.

parameters.requirement: valid license in the classification so advertised
parameters.exception: licensed building or engineering contractor may advertise as a general contractor
advertise_includes: card, sign, or device issued to any person
sign or marking on or in any building or structure
directory listing under construction/work of improvement

rules.applies_to: All contractors and unlicensed persons advertising construction work
rules.verbatim_quote: It is a misdemeanor for any person to advertise for construction or work of improvement covered by this chapter unless that person holds a valid license under this chapter in the classification so advertised, except that a licensed building or engineering contractor may advertise as a general contractor.
rules.notes: A tool can check ad copy/website service lists against the license's classifications.

rules.title: Fine for advertising without proper license: $700-$1,000
rules.plain_english: Advertising construction work without a license in the advertised classification carries a fine of $700 to $1,000, on top of any other punishment.
rules.applies_to: Persons violating B&P 7027.1
rules.verbatim_quote: A violation of this section is punishable by a fine of not less than seven hundred dollars ($700) and not more than one thousand dollars ($1,000), which fine shall be in addition to any other punishment imposed for a violation of this section.

verification.note: $700-$1,000 is the criminal fine. 16 CCR 884(a) (PDF page 540) sets a separate administrative citation range of $100-$1,000 for 7027.1.

rules.title: Unlicensed person may advertise only jobs under $1,000 with disclosure
rules.plain_english: Someone without a contractor's license may advertise construction work only if the total price for labor, materials and everything else on the project is less than $1,000 and the ad states that the person is not licensed.

parameters.required_ad_statement: person is not licensed under the Contractors State License Law

rules.applies_to: Unlicensed handypersons and similar
rules.verbatim_quote: a person who is not licensed pursuant to this chapter may advertise for construction work or a work of improvement covered by this chapter only if the aggregate contract price for labor, material, and all other items on a project or undertaking is less than one thousand dollars ($1,000) and the person states in the advertisement that the person is not licensed under this chapter.
rules.notes: Interacts with B&P 7048(c)(1): the minor-work exemption does not apply to a person who advertises in a way indicating they are a contractor or qualified to be one. The work must also meet all B&P 7048 conditions (no building permit required, not split, no employees).

verification.checked_against: 2026 CSLB Law Book (sources/lawbook.txt), PDF page 242 (B&P 7027.2; amended Stats 2024 ch 240, eff. Jan 1, 2025)

rules.title: Using a license number that is not yours, to defraud
rules.plain_english: Willfully using a contractor license number that is not your own currently valid license, with intent to defraud, is punishable by a fine up to $10,000, state prison or up to one year in county jail, or both.

parameters.conduct: willfully and intentionally uses, with intent to defraud, a license number not corresponding to a currently valid license held by that person
imprisonment_options: county jail not more than 1 year

rules.applies_to: Anyone, licensed or unlicensed
rules.verbatim_quote: Any person, licensed or unlicensed, who willfully and intentionally uses, with intent to defraud, a contractor’s license number that does not correspond to the number on a currently valid contractor’s license held by that person, is punishable by a fine not exceeding ten thousand dollars ($10,000)
rules.notes: Registrar may also cite an unlicensed violator under B&P 7028.7. A tool can verify that the license number on every document matches the company's own active license.

rules.title: Ads saying 'insured' must name the insurance type
rules.plain_english: If you advertise that you are 'insured', the ad must say what kind of insurance you carry, such as commercial general liability or workers' compensation (abbreviations are allowed). Otherwise it is cause for discipline. This covers business vehicles, signs, print, online and directory ads.

advertise_includes: sign or marking on building, structure or business vehicle

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors advertising
rules.verbatim_quote: It is a cause for discipline for any contractor to advertise that he or she is “insured” or has insurance without identifying in the advertisement the type of insurance, including, for example, “commercial general liability insurance” or “workers’ compensation insurance” that is carried by the contractor. The contractor may abbreviate the title of the type of insurance.
rules.notes: Ad-copy linter: flag 'insured' without a named coverage type.

rules.title: Do not advertise 'bonded' based on license or disciplinary bond
rules.plain_english: You may not advertise that you are 'bonded' if the bond you mean is just your required contractor's license bond or a disciplinary bond. Doing so is cause for discipline.
rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors advertising
rules.verbatim_quote: It is cause for discipline for a contractor to advertise that he or she is “bonded” if the reference is to a contractor’s license bond required pursuant to Section 7071.6 or to a disciplinary bond required pursuant to Section 7071.8.
rules.notes: 'Bonded' may be used only if it refers to some other bond (e.g., performance/payment bonding capacity); this inference is not stated in the text.

rules.title: C-27 landscape contractor may design its own systems
rules.plain_english: A landscape contractor working within its classification may design the systems or facilities that it will itself build and supervise.

parameters.design_allowed_for: systems or facilities for work to be performed and supervised by that contractor

rules.applies_to: C-27 landscape contractors
rules.verbatim_quote: A landscape contractor working within the classification for which the license is issued may design systems or facilities for work to be performed and supervised by that contractor.
rules.notes: Does not authorize work requiring a license under the Professional Engineers Act (B&P 7027.5(e)).

rules.title: C-27 may prime a pool/spa only inside its landscape project via one C-53
rules.plain_english: A C-27 landscape contractor may take a prime contract that includes a swimming pool, spa or hot tub only if it is part of the landscape project the C-27 is supervising, and the pool construction is subcontracted to a single licensed C-53 pool contractor (or the C-27 also holds C-53). The pool contractor may sub out individual components to properly licensed contractors.

conditions: improvements included within the landscape project the landscape contractor is supervising
pool/spa/hot tub construction subcontracted to a single licensed C-53 contractor, or performed by the landscape contractor if it also holds C-53

rules.applies_to: C-27 landscape contractors; owners contracting for landscape projects with pools
rules.verbatim_quote: A swimming pool, spa, or hot tub, provided that the improvements are included within the landscape project that the landscape contractor is supervising and the construction of any swimming pool, spa, or hot tub is subcontracted to a single licensed contractor holding a Swimming Pool (C-53) classification

rules.title: C-27 prime contracts: outdoor cooking center, fireplace, rainwater capture
rules.plain_english: A C-27 landscape contractor may take a prime contract for an outdoor cooking center or an outdoor fireplace (not attached to the house) if it is part of a residential landscape project the C-27 supervises, and for a rainwater capture system used only for landscape irrigation or a decorative water feature.

outdoor_cooking_center.condition: included within a residential landscape project the contractor is supervising
outdoor_cooking_center.definition: unenclosed area within a landscape used for cooking or preparation of food or beverages

conditions: included within a residential landscape project the contractor is supervising

allowed_uses: water supply for fountain, pond, or similar decorative water feature in a landscaping project

rules.applies_to: C-27 landscape contractors; residential owners
rules.verbatim_quote: An outdoor fireplace, provided that it is included within a residential landscape project that the contractor is supervising and is not attached to a dwelling.
rules.notes: See landscape-c27-out-of-scope-work for trade work outside C-27 scope on these items.

rules.title: C-27: out-of-scope work on cooking centers/fireplaces/rainwater needs proper license
rules.plain_english: On outdoor cooking center, outdoor fireplace or rainwater capture projects, any work outside the C-27 scope (e.g., gas, electrical) must be done by the C-27 only if it also holds the right specialty license or a B license; otherwise it must be done by a properly licensed specialty contractor or a B contractor working under the B rules. A C-27 may design and install all exterior rainwater capture components not attached to a structure.

parameters.rainwater_exception: C-27 may design and install all exterior components not part of or attached to a structure

rules.applies_to: C-27 landscape contractors
rules.verbatim_quote: If the landscape contractor neither holds an appropriate specialty license classification to perform the work nor is licensed as a General Building contractor, the work shall be performed by a Specialty contractor holding the appropriate license classification or by a General Building contractor performing work in accordance with the requirements of subdivision (b) of Section 7057.

rules.title: Contracting without a license (or under certain suspensions) is a crime
rules.plain_english: Unless exempt, it is a misdemeanor to engage in business or act as a contractor without a license, or while your license is suspended for failing to pay a CSLB civil penalty/comply with an order of correction (B&P 7090.1) or for unresolved outstanding final liabilities (B&P 7145.5).

conditions_any_of: license suspended under B&P 7090.1 (failure to pay civil penalty or comply with order of correction)
license suspended under B&P 7145.5 (failure to resolve outstanding final liabilities)

rules.applies_to: Anyone acting as a contractor in California
rules.verbatim_quote: Unless exempted from this chapter, it is a misdemeanor for a person to engage in the business of, or act in the capacity of, a contractor within this state under either of the following conditions: (1) The person is not licensed in accordance with this chapter.
rules.notes: A tool should verify license status (active, not suspended) at bid, contract signing and throughout performance.

rules.title: Unlicensed contracting: first conviction penalty
rules.plain_english: A first conviction for contracting without a license can bring a fine of up to $5,000, up to six months in county jail, or both.
rules.applies_to: Persons convicted under B&P 7028
rules.verbatim_quote: A first conviction for the offense described in this section is punishable by a fine not exceeding five thousand dollars ($5,000) or by imprisonment in a county jail not exceeding six months, or by both that fine and imprisonment.

verification.note: 16 CCR 884(a) (PDF page 540) lists a separate administrative citation range of $200-$8,000 for 7028.

rules.title: Unlicensed contracting: second conviction fine formula
rules.plain_english: On a second conviction the court must fine the greater of 20% of the contract price, 20% of all payments made to the unlicensed person, or $5,000, and jail for at least 90 days unless the court states reasons for a lesser sentence in an unusual case.

parameters.lesser_sentence_allowed: unusual case in interests of justice; court must state reasons on the record

rules.applies_to: Persons with a prior B&P 7028 conviction
rules.verbatim_quote: the court shall impose a fine of 20 percent of the contract price, or 20 percent of the aggregate payments made to, or at the direction of, the unlicensed person, or five thousand dollars ($5,000), whichever is greater, and, unless the sentence prescribed in subdivision (d) is imposed, the person shall be confined in a county jail for not less than 90 days
rules.notes: For hourly arrangements, see unlicensed-hourly-contract-price-definition.

rules.title: Unlicensed contracting: third or later conviction
rules.plain_english: A third or later conviction carries a fine from $5,000 up to the greater of $10,000 or 20% of the contract price/payments, plus 90 days to one year in county jail. The same enhanced penalty applies to anyone who was named on a revoked license and held responsible for the revocation.

parameters.also_applies_to: person named on a previously revoked license who was held responsible for the act or omission causing revocation (7028(e))

rules.applies_to: Repeat unlicensed contractors; persons tied to revoked licenses
rules.verbatim_quote: A third or subsequent conviction for the offense described in this section is punishable by a fine of not less than five thousand dollars ($5,000) nor more than the greater amount of ten thousand dollars ($10,000) or 20 percent of the contract price, or 20 percent of the aggregate payments made to, or at the direction of, the unlicensed person
rules.notes: Statute text: 'imprisonment in a county jail for not more than one year or less than 90 days'.

rules.title: 'Contract price' for hourly unlicensed work
rules.plain_english: When an unlicensed person agreed to supply materials and labor by the hour, the 'contract price' used for penalties equals the cost of materials and labor already furnished plus the cost to complete the work.

parameters.trigger: unlicensed person agreed to furnish materials and labor on an hourly basis

rules.applies_to: Penalty calculations under B&P 7028
rules.verbatim_quote: If the unlicensed person engaging in the business of or acting in the capacity of a contractor has agreed to furnish materials and labor on an hourly basis, “the contract price” for the purposes of this section means the aggregate sum of the cost of materials and labor furnished and the cost of completing the work to be performed.
rules.notes: B&P 7028.15(b) uses the same hourly definition for public-bid violations.

rules.title: 4-year window to prosecute unlicensed contracting
rules.plain_english: Criminal charges for unlicensed contracting must be filed within four years from the latest of: the contract proposal, the contract, completion, or abandonment of the work.

parameters.start_date: latest of contract proposal date, contract date, completion date, abandonment date

rules.applies_to: Owners/prosecutors evaluating unlicensed work
rules.verbatim_quote: an indictment for any violation of this section by an unlicensed person shall be found, or information or a complaint shall be filed, within four years from the date of the contract proposal, contract, completion, or abandonment of the work, whichever occurs last.
rules.notes: deadline = max(proposal, contract, completion, abandonment) + 4 years.

rules.title: Owner who used unlicensed contractor is a crime victim
rules.plain_english: If an unlicensed contractor is convicted, anyone who used their services is a crime victim eligible for restitution of economic losses, even if they knew the contractor was unlicensed.

parameters.eligible: person who utilized the services of the unlicensed person

rules.applies_to: Project owners and others who hired an unlicensed contractor
rules.verbatim_quote: For any conviction under this section, a person who utilized the services of the unlicensed person is a victim of crime and is eligible, pursuant to subdivision (f) of Section 1202.4 of the Penal Code, for restitution for economic losses, regardless of whether he or she had knowledge that the person was unlicensed.
rules.notes: Subdivision (i) says these changes are declaratory of existing law.

rules.title: Asbestos, hazardous-substance removal and UST work require certification
rules.plain_english: Any contractor, licensed or not, commits a misdemeanor by doing asbestos-related work without CSLB asbestos certification (B&P 7058.5), doing hazardous substance removal or remedial action without certification (B&P 7058.7), or bidding on, installing or removing an underground storage tank without certification (B&P 7058.7), unless exempt.

work_requiring_certification.work: bid for, install, or remove underground storage tank

rules.applies_to: Contractors doing abatement, hazardous remediation or UST work; GCs bidding such work
rules.verbatim_quote: It is a misdemeanor for any contractor, whether licensed or unlicensed, to perform or engage in asbestos-related work, as defined in Section 6501.8 of the Labor Code, without certification pursuant to Section 7058.5 of this code, or to perform or engage in a removal or remedial action, as defined in subdivision (d) of Section 7058.7
rules.notes: Certification requirements themselves (B&P 7058.5-7058.7) are outside this chunk. Note that merely bidding on UST work without certification is covered.

rules.title: Penalties for uncertified asbestos/HAZ/UST work
rules.plain_english: First offense: fine of $1,000 to $3,000 and possible license suspension or revocation. Subsequent offense: fine of $3,000 to $5,000 or up to one year in county jail or both, plus mandatory action to suspend or revoke the license.

subsequent_offense.license_action: mandatory action to suspend or revoke

rules.applies_to: Contractors violating B&P 7028.1
rules.verbatim_quote: Conviction of a first offense is punishable by a fine of not less than one thousand dollars ($1,000) or more than three thousand dollars ($3,000), and by possible revocation or suspension of any contractor’s license.
rules.notes: Subsequent offense text: 'a fine of not less than three thousand dollars ($3,000) or more than five thousand dollars ($5,000), or imprisonment in the county jail not exceeding one year, or both ... and a mandatory action to suspend or revoke any contractor's license.'

verification.note: These are criminal fines. 16 CCR 884(a) (PDF page 540) lists a separate administrative citation range of $1,000-$8,000 for 7028.1.

rules.title: CSLB may seek court injunction against violators
rules.plain_english: CSLB can go to superior court (through the Attorney General or district attorney) for a TRO or injunction against a licensee whose violations may substantially injure someone, or against any unlicensed person violating the law, whether or not anyone is injured.

parameters.against_licensee_when: violation whereby another person may be substantially injured
parameters.against_unlicensed_when: any violation, whether or not there is substantial injury
parameters.venue: superior court of county where act occurred, or where person has a place of business or resides

rules.applies_to: Licensees and unlicensed persons
rules.verbatim_quote: the registrar may, either through the Attorney General or through the district attorney of the county in which the act, practice, or transaction is alleged to have been committed, apply to the superior court of that county or any other county in which such person maintains a place of business or resides, for an injunction

rules.title: Licensed contractors and consumers can enjoin unlicensed competitors
rules.plain_english: A licensed contractor, a contractors' association, an affected consumer, a district attorney or the Attorney General can get a court injunction stopping a continuing violation by someone with no contractor's license in any classification, without having to prove irreparable injury.

parameters.defendant: person who does not hold a state contractor's license in any classification

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors facing unlicensed competition; consumers
rules.verbatim_quote: The plaintiff in any such action shall not be required to prove irreparable injury.

rules.title: Officers/qualifiers of a licensed company can't contract individually
rules.plain_english: Being a partner, officer, director, manager, RME/RMO/RMM or other listed personnel of a licensed company does not let you contract on your own. You need your own license in good standing to do work individually.

covered_roles: any individual listed in personnel of record
parameters.prohibited: individually engage in business or act as contractor without own license in good standing

rules.applies_to: Personnel of record of licensed entities
rules.verbatim_quote: an individual who is listed in the personnel of record of, a licensed partnership, corporation, limited liability company, firm, association or other organization to individually engage in the business or individually act in the capacity of a contractor within this state without having a license in good standing to so engage or act.
rules.notes: Statute begins 'It is unlawful for a person who is or has been a partner, officer, director, manager, responsible managing employee...'.

rules.title: CSLB citation for unlicensed activity: $1,500-$15,000 (from July 1, 2026)
rules.plain_english: When CSLB has probable cause that someone is contracting (or selling home improvements) without a license or registration in good standing, it must issue a written citation with an order of abatement and a civil penalty of $1,500 to $15,000. These penalties are in addition to any civil or criminal remedies.

citation_contents: written description of basis with particularity
covers: acting as contractor without license in good standing
acting as home improvement salesperson without registration

inflation_adjustment.index: CPI per Revenue and Taxation Code 2212

rules.applies_to: Unlicensed contractors and unregistered salespersons
rules.verbatim_quote: each citation shall contain an order of abatement and an assessment of a civil penalty in an amount not less than fifteen hundred dollars ($1,500) nor more than fifteen thousand dollars ($15,000).
rules.effective: Effective January 1, 2026; operative July 1, 2026 (added by Stats 2025 ch 233 § 2, SB 779)
rules.notes: Replaces prior version (see unlicensed-citation-civil-penalty-pre-july-2026). Inflation adjustments to the minimum are discretionary ('may adjust'). 16 CCR 884(a) (PDF page 540) still lists $200-$15,000 for 7028.7; the statutory $1,500 minimum operative July 1, 2026 controls. 16 CCR 884(c) (PDF page 542): where a citation lists several violations on the same project, the total assessment for 7028.7 may not exceed $15,000.

verification.checked_against: 2026 CSLB Law Book (sources/lawbook.txt), PDF pages 248-250 (B&P 7028.6; B&P 7028.7 operative July 1, 2026); 16 CCR 884 (PDF pages 540, 542)
verification.correction: Amounts ($1,500-$15,000), CPI adjustment (every 5 years, minimums only, $100 rounding) and quote confirmed. "effective" said "July 1, 2026"; the book says effective January 1, 2026, operative July 1, 2026. Fixed. Added a note that 16 CCR 884(a) still shows the old $200 minimum and that 884(c) caps the per-citation total at $15,000.

rules.title: Prior citation range $200-$15,000 (through June 30, 2026)
rules.plain_english: Under the version of B&P 7028.7 in effect until July 1, 2026, the civil penalty in a citation for unlicensed activity ranged from $200 to $15,000.
rules.applies_to: Citations issued under the version in effect before July 1, 2026
rules.verbatim_quote: each citation shall contain an order of abatement and an assessment of a civil penalty in an amount not less than two hundred dollars ($200) nor more than fifteen thousand dollars ($15,000).
rules.notes: Historical only; which version applies to conduct before July 1, 2026 but cited after is not addressed in the text.

verification.checked_against: 2026 CSLB Law Book (sources/lawbook.txt), PDF pages 248-249 (B&P 7028.7(c), version effective until July 1, 2026)
verification.note: Matches 16 CCR 884(a) (PDF page 540) range for 7028.7 ($200-$15,000). Repealed July 1, 2026 by its own subdivision (f); historical only as of 2026-11-25.

rules.title: CSLB 72-hour notice to public entity awarding to unlicensed contractor
rules.plain_english: Within 72 hours of learning that a public entity intends to award, or has awarded, a contract to an unlicensed contractor, CSLB must warn the entity in writing that a citation may issue. If the entity awards anyway, CSLB may cite the responsible public officer or employee.

parameters.trigger: registrar receives notice that a public entity intends to award or has awarded a contract to an unlicensed contractor
parameters.follow_on: registrar may cite responsible officer or employee under B&P 7028.15

rules.applies_to: Public agencies awarding construction contracts; bidders
rules.verbatim_quote: Within 72 hours of receiving notice that a public entity is intending to award, or has awarded, a contract to an unlicensed contractor, the registrar shall give written notice to the public entity that a citation may be issued if a contract is awarded to an unlicensed contractor.
rules.effective: Same text in version effective until July 1, 2026 and version operative July 1, 2026
rules.notes: Competing bidders can report an unlicensed apparent low bidder to CSLB to trigger this notice.

verification.checked_against: 2026 CSLB Law Book (sources/lawbook.txt), PDF pages 248-249 (B&P 7028.7(b), both versions)
verification.note: Same 72-hour text appears in the repealed version (PDF pages 248-249) and the version operative July 1, 2026 (PDF page 249).

rules.title: Citation may be served by certified mail
rules.plain_english: A citation for unlicensed activity can be served by certified mail to the person's last known business or residence address.

parameters.address: last known business address or residence address

rules.applies_to: Persons cited under B&P 7028.7
rules.verbatim_quote: Service of a citation issued under Section 7028.7 may be made by certified mail at the last known business address or residence address of the person cited.
rules.notes: Service date starts the 15-working-day appeal clock (B&P 7028.10-7028.11).

rules.title: Deadline for CSLB to issue unlicensed-activity citation
rules.plain_english: CSLB must issue an unlicensed-activity citation within four years after the act or omission, or within 18 months after the complaint was filed, whichever is later.
rules.applies_to: Unlicensed persons; owners filing complaints
rules.verbatim_quote: A citation under Section 7028.7 shall be issued by the registrar within four years after the act or omission that is the basis for the citation or within 18 months after the date of the filing of the complaint with the registrar, whichever is later.
rules.notes: deadline = max(act_date + 4 years, complaint_filed_date + 18 months).

rules.title: Contest an unlicensed-activity citation within 15 days of service (B&P 7099.8; 7028.10 says 15 working days)
rules.plain_english: B&P 7028.10 and 7028.11 give 15 working days after service to appeal an unlicensed-activity citation (the violations, the abatement order, or the penalty amount), extendable by CSLB for good cause; if you miss it, the citation becomes a final order no court or agency can review. But B&P 7099.8(a), which applies "notwithstanding any other law" to 7028.7 citations, requires a written request for an administrative hearing within 15 days after service, and it does not say working days. In the same 15 days you may instead (or also) ask in writing for an informal citation conference. Treat 15 calendar days from service as the deadline.

parameters.day_type: calendar days (safe reading; B&P 7099.8(a) says "within 15 days" and overrides "notwithstanding any other law")
parameters.consequence_if_missed: citation deemed final order not subject to review by any court or agency
parameters.extension: registrar may extend for good cause

overriding_rule_b_p_7099_8.text_controls: B&P 7099.8(a) applies "notwithstanding any other law" to citations under 7028.7

informal_citation_conference_option.request_to: chief of the enforcement division or designee, in writing

parameters.safe_deadline: 15 calendar days after service of the citation

rules.applies_to: Persons cited under B&P 7028.7
rules.verbatim_quote: If within 15 working days after service of the citation, the person cited fails to notify the registrar that he or she intends to appeal the citation, the citation shall be deemed a final order of the registrar and not subject to review by any court or agency. The 15-day period may be extended by the registrar for good cause.
rules.notes: Do not compute this deadline in working days. 7099.8 (added 2019) is later and says "notwithstanding any other law"; 15 calendar days is the safe date. After an informal conference, an affirmed or modified citation is mailed within 10 days and may be contested by written hearing request within 30 days after its service (7099.8(b)(3)-(4)).

verification.checked_against: 2026 CSLB Law Book (sources/lawbook.txt), PDF pages 250-251 (B&P 7028.10, 7028.11) and PDF pages 342-343 (B&P 7099.8)
verification.correction: The 7028.10/7028.11 quote ("15 working days") is accurate, but the rule left out B&P 7099.8(a) (PDF page 342): "Notwithstanding any other law, if a person cited pursuant to Section 7028.7 ... wishes to contest the citation, that person shall, within 15 days after service of the citation, file in writing a request for an administrative hearing". It does not say working days. Added 7099.8 parameters (including the informal-conference option) and set the safe deadline to 15 calendar days after service. Replaced the note that told tools to count working days. Renamed the working_days parameter so that days = 15 with day_type = calendar; the 7028.10 working-day figure is kept as b_p_7028_10_7028_11_text_working_days for reference. Retitled the rule.

rules.title: Hearing on a contested citation
rules.plain_english: If you timely contest the citation, CSLB must give you a hearing under the Administrative Procedure Act and then issue a decision affirming, modifying or vacating the citation.

parameters.trigger: timely notice of intent to contest

rules.applies_to: Persons cited under B&P 7028.7
rules.verbatim_quote: If the person cited under Section 7028.7 timely notifies the registrar that he or she intends to contest the citation, the registrar shall afford an opportunity for a hearing.

rules.title: Collection of citation penalties: court judgment, collectors, 4/10-year windows
rules.plain_english: After review is exhausted, CSLB can get a superior court judgment for the penalty and an order to obey the abatement order. It can hand collection to a collection agency (you pay the collection costs) or sell the penalty rights. CSLB has 4 years from the final order to collect, or 10 years from a court judgment.

registrar_may: apply to superior court for judgment and compliance order
assign rights to civil penalty for adequate consideration

rules.applies_to: Persons with final unlicensed-activity citations
rules.verbatim_quote: the registrar or his or her designee or assignee shall have four years from the date of the final order to collect civil penalties except that the registrar or his or her designee or assignee shall have 10 years from the date of the judgment to enforce civil penalties on citations that have been converted to judgments
rules.notes: Overrides Code of Civil Procedure 340(a)-(b).

rules.title: Part of penalty may be waived if you get licensed
rules.plain_english: CSLB may waive part of an unlicensed-activity civil penalty if the cited person completes all requirements and is issued a contractor's license. Any outstanding injury to the public must be settled before the license is issued.

conditions: cited person satisfactorily completes all licensing requirements and is issued a license
outstanding injury to the public satisfactorily settled before license issuance

rules.applies_to: Cited unlicensed persons who apply for a license
rules.verbatim_quote: the registrar may waive part of the civil penalty if the person against whom the civil penalty is assessed satisfactorily completes all the requirements for, and is issued, a contractor’s license. Any outstanding injury to the public shall be satisfactorily settled prior to issuance of the license.
rules.notes: Waiver amount not specified.

rules.title: License required to bid public works
rules.plain_english: It is a misdemeanor to submit a bid to a public agency for contracting work without a license, unless you are specifically exempt or the bid is on a state project under Public Contract Code 10164 or a local project under Public Contract Code 20103.5.

exceptions: person particularly exempted from the chapter
state project governed by Public Contract Code 10164
local agency project governed by Public Contract Code 20103.5

rules.applies_to: Bidders on public agency projects
rules.verbatim_quote: It is a misdemeanor for any person to submit a bid to a public agency in order to engage in the business or act in the capacity of a contractor within this state without having a license therefor, except in any of the following cases:
rules.notes: PCC 10164 and 20103.5 (in the book's Appendix, not this chunk) cover projects with federal funds where licensure may be required at award rather than at bid.

rules.title: Repeat unlicensed public bid: 20% or $4,500 fine
rules.plain_english: If previously convicted of bidding public work without a license, the court must impose a fine of the greater of 20% of the contract price or $4,500, or 10 days to 6 months in county jail, or both.

parameters.hourly_contract_price: cost of materials and labor furnished + cost of completing the work

rules.applies_to: Repeat violators of B&P 7028.15
rules.verbatim_quote: the court shall impose a fine of 20 percent of the price of the contract under which the unlicensed person performed contracting work, or four thousand five hundred dollars ($4,500), whichever is greater, or imprisonment in the county jail for not less than 10 days nor more than six months, or both.
rules.notes: Penalty for a first conviction is not specified in this section (general misdemeanor penalties would apply).

rules.title: Unlicensed public bid is nonresponsive; contract void
rules.plain_english: A public agency must reject an unlicensed contractor's bid as nonresponsive. A local agency must verify the contractor was properly licensed when it bid before awarding a contract or issuing a purchase order. Any contract or purchase order issued to an unlicensed contractor is void, and a public officer who knowingly awards one can be cited.

parameters.local_agency_verification: verify contractor was properly licensed when bid was submitted, before award or purchase order
parameters.public_officer_sanction: citation if knowingly awards to unlicensed contractor (penalties per B&P 7028.7-7028.13)

rules.applies_to: Public agencies, bidders, competing bidders
rules.verbatim_quote: a bid submitted to a public agency by a contractor who is not licensed in accordance with this chapter shall be considered nonresponsive and shall be rejected by the public agency. Unless one of the foregoing exceptions applies, a local public agency shall, before awarding a contract or issuing a purchase order, verify that the contractor was properly licensed when the contractor submitted the bid
rules.notes: Also: 'Any contract awarded to, or any purchase order issued to, a contractor who is not licensed pursuant to this chapter is void.'

rules.title: Public officer safe harbor if CSLB doesn't answer in 3 business days
rules.plain_english: A public officer or employee cannot be cited for awarding to an unlicensed contractor if the agency asked CSLB to verify the license status and CSLB did not respond within three business days. A phone response from CSLB counts.

parameters.trigger: public employee, officer, or agency inquiry to CSLB to verify license status
parameters.effect: no citation if board fails to respond within 3 business days

rules.applies_to: Public agency staff awarding contracts
rules.verbatim_quote: A public employee or officer shall not be subject to a citation pursuant to this section if the public employee, officer, or employing agency made an inquiry to the board for the purposes of verifying the license status of any person or contractor and the board failed to respond to the inquiry within three business days.
rules.notes: A tool can log date/time of license verification inquiries.

rules.title: Joint venture bids: each member individually licensed at bid
rules.plain_english: A joint venture license is not required at the time of a public bid, but every party submitting the joint venture bid must be individually licensed when the bid is made. Licensed architects, land surveyors and engineers may form joint ventures with licensed contractors within their practices.
rules.applies_to: Contractors bidding public work as joint ventures
rules.verbatim_quote: This section shall not apply to a joint venture license, as required by Section 7029.1. However, at the time of making a bid as a joint venture, each person submitting the bid shall be subject to this section with respect to his or her individual licensure.
rules.notes: A JV license is still required before being awarded the contract jointly (B&P 7029.1).

rules.title: Unlicensed disaster repair: felony-level penalties
rules.plain_english: Contracting without a license to repair damage from a natural disaster declared a state of emergency by the Governor (or an emergency/major disaster declared by the President) is punishable by a fine up to $10,000 and/or 16 months, 2 or 3 years under Penal Code 1170(h), or a fine up to $1,000 and/or up to one year in county jail. Anyone who hired the unlicensed contractor is a crime victim.

parameters.trigger: unlicensed offer or performance of repairs/improvements to residential or nonresidential structure or property, or grounds, for damage caused by a declared natural disaster
declarations: Presidential emergency or major disaster declaration

rules.applies_to: Unlicensed persons doing disaster repair; owners of disaster-damaged property
rules.verbatim_quote: shall be punished by a fine up to ten thousand dollars ($10,000), or by imprisonment pursuant to subdivision (h) of Section 1170 of the Penal Code for 16 months, or for two or three years, or by both that fine and imprisonment, or by a fine up to one thousand dollars ($1,000), or by imprisonment in a county jail not exceeding one year, or by both that fine and imprisonment.
rules.notes: Book cross-references Penal Code 670, 667.16 and 551 (Appendix).

rules.title: Ignoring a final citation is a misdemeanor (unlicensed)
rules.plain_english: An unlicensed individual who fails to comply with a citation after it becomes final commits a misdemeanor.

parameters.trigger: failure to comply with citation after it is final

fine_distribution.city_attorney_action: city treasurer for city attorney use

rules.applies_to: Cited unlicensed persons
rules.verbatim_quote: The failure of an unlicensed individual to comply with a citation after it is final is a misdemeanor.

rules.title: Joint venture license requirements
rules.plain_english: A joint venture license is issued to a combination of individuals/entities that each hold a current, active license in good standing. It can be issued in any classification held by at least one member, and it is automatically suspended whenever any member lacks a current, active license in good standing.

parameters.member_requirement: each member holds current, active license in good standing
parameters.available_classifications: any classification in which at least one member is licensed
parameters.automatic_suspension_trigger: any member does not hold current, active license in good standing

rules.applies_to: Contractors forming joint ventures
rules.verbatim_quote: A joint venture license is a license issued to any combination of individuals, corporations, limited liability companies, partnerships, or other joint ventures, each of which holds a current, active license in good standing. A joint venture license may be issued in any classification in which at least one of the entities is licensed.
rules.notes: Tool check: monitor each JV member's license status; any lapse suspends the JV license.

rules.title: Need a JV license to be awarded a contract jointly
rules.plain_english: Two or more separately licensed contractors may bid jointly, but they must obtain a joint venture license before being awarded a contract jointly or otherwise acting together as a contractor. Not getting the JV license does not excuse bid-default penalties. Violation is cause for discipline.

jv_license_required_before: otherwise acting jointly as a contractor

rules.applies_to: Contractors teaming on projects
rules.verbatim_quote: it is unlawful for any two or more licensees, each of whom has been issued a license to act separately in the capacity of a contractor within this state, to be awarded a contract jointly or otherwise act as a contractor without first having secured a joint venture license in accordance with the provisions of this chapter.
rules.notes: Under B&P 7031(a), individually licensed contractors who fail to get a JV license are not barred from suing for payment.

rules.title: Plumbing, sign and well-drilling vehicles: name, address, license # (1.5 in)
rules.plain_english: C-36 plumbing, C-45 sign and C-57 well-drilling contractors must show their name, permanent business address and license number on each side of every commercially registered business vehicle, in letters and numbers at least 1.5 inches high. Water-well drill rigs must be marked too.

parameters.also_applies_to: any drill rig used for drilling water wells

rules.applies_to: C-36, C-45, C-57 licensees
rules.verbatim_quote: his or her name, permanent business address, and contractor’s license number, all in letters and numerals not less than 1½ inches high.

verification.note: 16 CCR 884(a) (PDF page 540) sets an administrative citation range of $100-$500 for 7029.5.

rules.title: All other contractors: business name and license # on vehicles
rules.plain_english: Every other licensed contractor must display its business name and license number in or on each commercially registered vehicle used in its construction business, clearly visible, in at least 72-point type or 3/4 inch high and wide.

parameters.vehicles: each motor vehicle used in construction business for which a commercial vehicle registration fee has been paid
parameters.placement: in or on the vehicle, clearly visible location

rules.title: CSLB notice in prime contracts (non-home-improvement), 10-point
rules.plain_english: Every written contract where you are the prime contractor (other than home improvement and service-and-repair contracts) must include the CSLB licensing/complaint-deadline statement in at least 10-point type. Failure is cause for discipline.

A complaint regarding a latent act or omission pertaining to structural defects must be filed within 10 years of the date of the alleged violation. Any questions concerning a contractor may be referred to the Registrar, Contractors State License Board, P.O. Box 26000, Sacramento, CA 95826.

rules.applies_to: Licensed prime contractors on commercial, public and new-construction contracts

rules.notes: Full mandatory text is in parameters.required_text exactly as printed; generate verbatim.

rules.title: CSLB information notice in home improvement and service/repair contracts, 12-point
rules.plain_english: Every home improvement contract and service-and-repair contract must include the 'Information about the Contractors State License Board (CSLB)' statement in at least 12-point type. Failure is cause for discipline.

parameters.required_text:
Information about the Contractors State License Board (CSLB): CSLB is the state consumer protection agency that licenses and regulates construction contractors.
Contact CSLB for information about the licensed contractor you are considering, including information about disclosable complaints, disciplinary actions and civil judgments that are reported to CSLB.
Use only licensed contractors. If you file a complaint against a licensed contractor within the legal deadline (usually four years), CSLB has authority to investigate the complaint. If you use an unlicensed contractor, CSLB may not be able to help you resolve your complaint. Your only remedy may be in civil court, and you may be liable for damages arising out of any injuries to the unlicensed contractor or the unlicensed contractor’s employees.
For more information:
Visit CSLB’s internet website at www.cslb.ca.gov
Call CSLB at 800-321-CSLB (2752)
Write CSLB at P.O. Box 26000, Sacramento, CA 95826.

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors writing home improvement or service and repair contracts
rules.verbatim_quote: Every person licensed pursuant to this chapter shall include the following statement in at least 12-point type in all home improvement contracts written pursuant to Section 7151.2 and service and repair contracts written pursuant to Section 7159.10:
rules.notes: Full mandatory text is in parameters.required_text exactly as printed (line breaks as in the book). Other HIC content requirements are in B&P 7159 (outside this chunk).

rules.title: Disclose prior suspensions/revocations before residential contracts
rules.plain_english: If your license has been suspended or revoked two or more times within eight years, before contracting for work on residential property with four or fewer units you must disclose every disciplinary suspension or revocation in the last eight years (even if stayed), in a pre-contract document such as a bid or estimate, in 10-point bold capital letters or 8-point bold red print.

parameters.property_type: residential property with four or fewer units
parameters.timing: document provided prior to entering into the contract
parameters.content: any disciplinary license suspension or revocation during the last eight years resulting from any violation of the chapter, whether or not stayed

rules.applies_to: Contractors with 2+ suspensions/revocations in 8 years working on 1-4 unit residential
rules.verbatim_quote: A contractor, who has his or her license suspended or revoked two or more times within an eight-year period, shall disclose either in capital letters in 10-point roman boldface type or in contrasting red print in at least 8-point roman boldface type, in a document provided prior to entering into a contract to perform work on residential property with four or fewer units
rules.notes: Tool check: count license suspensions/revocations in a rolling 8-year window; auto-insert disclosure into bids/estimates when >= 2.

rules.title: Penalties for failing the prior-discipline disclosure
rules.plain_english: Failing to make the required prior-discipline disclosure costs $1,000 for the first violation, $2,500 for the second, $5,000 plus a one-year license suspension for the third, and license revocation for the fourth.
rules.applies_to: Contractors violating B&P 7030.1
rules.verbatim_quote: (1) A penalty of one thousand dollars ($1,000) shall be assessed for the first violation. (2) A penalty of two thousand five hundred dollars ($2,500) shall be assessed for the second violation. (3) A penalty of five thousand dollars ($5,000) shall be assessed for a third violation in addition to a one-year suspension of license by operation of law.
rules.notes: Fourth violation: 'shall result in the revocation of license in accordance with this chapter.'
