rules.title: License number on all contracts, subcontracts, bid calls and ads
rules.plain_english: You must put your contractor's license number on all construction contracts, all subcontracts and calls for bids, and all forms of advertising.

documents: all forms of advertising (as prescribed by the registrar)

rules.applies_to: All licensed contractors
rules.verbatim_quote: Every person licensed pursuant to this chapter shall include his license number in: (a) all construction contracts; (b) subcontracts and calls for bid; and (c) all forms of advertising, as prescribed by the registrar of contractors, used by such a person.
rules.notes: Template check: license number field required on every contract, subcontract, bid invitation, website and ad.

rules.title: No lawsuit for payment unless licensed at all times
rules.plain_english: A contractor cannot sue or recover payment for work that needs a license unless it alleges (and if challenged, proves) it was properly licensed the entire time it performed the work, no matter how good its claim otherwise is. Exception: individually licensed contractors who only failed to get a joint venture license.

parameters.requirement: duly licensed contractor at all times during performance of the act or contract
parameters.exception: contractors each individually licensed but who failed to comply with B&P 7029 (joint venture license)

rules.applies_to: Contractors and subcontractors seeking payment through courts or arbitration
rules.verbatim_quote: no person engaged in the business or acting in the capacity of a contractor, may bring or maintain any action, or recover in law or equity in any action, in any court of this state for the collection of compensation for the performance of any act or contract where a license is required by this chapter without alleging that they were a duly licensed contractor at all times
rules.notes: A license lapse (expiration, suspension, classification gap) at any point during performance can forfeit the right to be paid. Track license status daily over each project's performance period.

rules.title: Owner can recover everything paid to an unlicensed contractor
rules.plain_english: Anyone who used an unlicensed contractor can sue to get back all compensation paid to that contractor for the work.

parameters.plaintiff: person who utilized the services of an unlicensed contractor
parameters.recoverable_amount: all compensation paid to the unlicensed contractor for performance of any act or contract

rules.applies_to: Project owners, GCs who paid unlicensed subs
rules.verbatim_quote: a person who utilizes the services of an unlicensed contractor may bring an action in any court of competent jurisdiction in this state to recover all compensation paid to the unlicensed contractor for performance of any act or contract.
rules.notes: Applies to GCs as well: a GC that paid an unlicensed sub can be sued for disgorgement, and a GC can seek disgorgement from an unlicensed sub. Calculation = sum of all payments made.

verification.note: The notes field's statement about GCs and unlicensed subs is case-law interpretation; it is not stated in the 7031(b) text.

rules.title: Unlicensed contractor's security interest is unenforceable
rules.plain_english: Any security interest taken to secure payment for licensed work is unenforceable if the contractor was not properly licensed the whole time it did the work.

parameters.affected: security interest securing payment for work requiring a license
parameters.condition: performer not duly licensed at all times during performance

rules.applies_to: Contractors relying on security interests for payment
rules.verbatim_quote: A security interest taken to secure any payment for the performance of any act or contract for which a license is required by this chapter is unenforceable if the person performing the act or contract was not a duly licensed contractor at all times during the performance of the act or contract.
rules.notes: The text says 'security interest'; whether this reaches mechanics liens is not stated here (mechanics lien rules are in the Civil Code).

rules.title: Prove licensure with a CSLB verified certificate
rules.plain_english: If your licensure is challenged in a payment suit, you must prove it with a verified certificate of licensure from CSLB showing you held the proper classification the entire time. The burden of proof is on the contractor; the challenger does not have to produce a certificate.

parameters.trigger: licensure or proper licensure is controverted
parameters.document: verified certificate of licensure from CSLB
parameters.certificate_must_show: duly licensed in the proper classification at all times during performance of any act or contract covered by the action

rules.applies_to: Contractors suing for payment
rules.verbatim_quote: proof of licensure pursuant to this section shall be made by production of a verified certificate of licensure from the Contractors State License Board which establishes that the individual or entity bringing the action was duly licensed in the proper classification of contractors at all times during the performance of any act or contract covered by the action.
rules.notes: Proper classification matters: being licensed but in the wrong classification may fail this test.

rules.title: Substantial compliance: narrow 3-part exception
rules.plain_english: A court may excuse a licensing lapse only if, after an evidentiary hearing, the contractor shows it (1) was licensed in California before performing the work, (2) acted reasonably and in good faith to keep proper licensure, and (3) acted promptly and in good faith to fix the problem once it learned of it. A contractor that was never licensed in California cannot use this exception.

all_required: duly licensed in California prior to performance of the act or contract
acted reasonably and in good faith to maintain proper licensure
acted promptly and in good faith to remedy the failure upon learning of it

rules.applies_to: Contractors whose license lapsed during a project
rules.verbatim_quote: The judicial doctrine of substantial compliance shall not apply under this section where the person who engaged in the business or acted in the capacity of a contractor has never been a duly licensed contractor in this state.
rules.notes: 1994 amendments do not apply to actions/arbitrations commenced before January 1, 1995 (7031(f)).

rules.title: Signed license statement (or exemption basis) with every building permit
rules.plain_english: Cities and counties must require each building permit applicant to file a signed statement giving their contractor license number and stating it is in full force, or, if exempt, the basis for the exemption. Violating this carries a civil penalty of up to $500.

parameters.trigger: application for permit for construction, alteration, improvement, demolition or repair of a building or structure
parameters.document: statement prepared and signed by applicant
contents_if_licensed: statement license is in full force and effect

rules.applies_to: Permit applicants (contractors and owner-builders)
rules.verbatim_quote: each applicant for such a permit file as a condition precedent to the issuance of a permit a statement which he has prepared and signed stating that the applicant is licensed under the provisions of this chapter, giving the number of the license and stating that it is in full force and effect, or, if the applicant is exempt from the provisions of this chapter, the basis for the alleged exemption.
rules.notes: Owner-builders typically cite B&P 7044 as the exemption basis. A false statement is the applicant's violation.

verification.note: $500 maximum civil penalty confirmed; consistent with 16 CCR 884(a) (PDF page 540) range of $100-$500 for 7031.5.

rules.title: Local permits/inspections allowed; no local contractor qualification rules
rules.plain_english: Cities and counties may regulate installation quality through permits, inspections and plan approval before construction, and may send complaints about code violations to CSLB, which get priority. But cities and counties may not set their own qualifications to be in the contracting business.

local_powers: require submission and approval of plans and specifications before construction
enforce local health and safety laws
direct complaints to CSLB registrar about code violations (priority processing)
parameters.local_prohibition: enact regulations relating to qualifications to engage in the business of contracting

rules.applies_to: Contractors and owners dealing with local building departments
rules.verbatim_quote: Nothing contained in this section shall be construed as authorizing a city or county to enact regulations relating to the qualifications necessary to engage in the business of contracting.
rules.notes: Local code-violation findings can become CSLB complaints.

rules.title: City business license: signed CSLB license statement or exemption proof
rules.plain_english: A city that requires a business license for contracting businesses must require each licensee or applicant (new or renewal) to file a signed statement that it holds a CSLB license in full force, or proof of the facts supporting an exemption.

parameters.trigger: city or city and county requires a business license as a condition of engaging in a business regulated by the CSLL
parameters.document: signed statement that applicant is licensed under the CSLL and license is in full force and effect
parameters.alternative: proof of facts entitling applicant to exemption

rules.applies_to: Contractors obtaining or renewing city business licenses
rules.verbatim_quote: a signed statement that such licensee or applicant is licensed under the provisions of this chapter and stating that the license is in full force and effect, or, if such licensee or applicant is exempt from the provisions of this chapter, he shall furnish proof of the facts which entitle him to such exemption.

rules.title: No void indemnity clauses (Civ. Code 2782) in subcontracts
rules.plain_english: A contractor may not put into a subcontract with a licensed subcontractor, or be a party to, any clause that is void or unenforceable under Civil Code 2782 (the anti-indemnity statute).

parameters.prohibited_clause: any provision, clause, covenant, or agreement void or unenforceable under Civil Code 2782

rules.applies_to: General contractors and upper-tier subcontractors drafting subcontracts
rules.verbatim_quote: No contractor that is required to be licensed under this chapter shall insert in any contract, or be a party, with a subcontractor that is licensed under this chapter to any contract which contains, a provision, clause, covenant, or agreement which is void or unenforceable under Section 2782 of the Civil Code.
rules.notes: Civil Code 2782/2782.6 are in the book's Appendix (not this chunk). Subcontract template linter should flag broad-form indemnity for active negligence/sole negligence, etc.

rules.title: Don't demand lien waivers that violate Civ. Code 8122
rules.plain_english: A contractor may not require a subcontractor, employee or supplier to waive lien rights in violation of Civil Code 8122 (which generally requires the statutory waiver and release forms).

parameters.prohibited: requiring a waiver of lien rights in violation of Civil Code 8122

rules.applies_to: General contractors and upper-tier subcontractors
rules.verbatim_quote: No contractor that is required to be licensed under this chapter shall require a waiver of lien rights from any subcontractor, employee, or supplier in violation of Section 8122 of the Civil Code.
rules.notes: Civil Code 8122 content is not reproduced in this chunk; the parenthetical about statutory forms is general background, not read here.

rules.title: Specialty contractor: max one sub in its own classification per project
rules.plain_english: A specialty (C) contractor may not subcontract work on a single project to more than one subcontractor holding the same classification as itself, unless the subcontractor uses its own W-2 employees for that work on the project, or the specialty contractor is signatory to a collective bargaining agreement covering that work that addresses subcontracting.

exceptions_any_of: subcontractor classifies the individuals performing that classification's work on the project as employees (not independent contractors) under the Labor Code
specialty contractor is signatory to a bona fide CBA covering the work type and addressing subcontracting

rules.applies_to: C-class specialty contractors subcontracting their own trade
rules.verbatim_quote: A specialty contractor shall not enter into a contract for the performance of work on the same single project or undertaking with more than one subcontractor in the same license classification as the specialty contractor offering the contract, unless either of the following requirements are satisfied:
rules.notes: Tool check per project: count subs whose classification equals the hiring specialty contractor's; if > 1, require employee-status or CBA attestation for each.

rules.title: Attorney General can pursue license discipline for unpaid wages
rules.plain_english: The Attorney General may sue to suspend, revoke or deny a contractor's license if the contractor failed to pay workers full wages owed, has an unpaid wage judgment, or violated a wage-payment injunction or court order. The AG must notify CSLB at least 30 days before filing; CSLB may intervene within 60 days. A good-faith mistake about which wage rate applies (including prevailing wage) is not a violation.

grounds_any_of: failed to pay workers full wages owed under state law
has not fulfilled a wage judgment
violating an injunction or court order regarding payment of wages

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors and applicants with wage-payment issues
rules.verbatim_quote: The civil action shall be brought on the grounds that a person has failed to pay its workers the full amount of wages that the workers are entitled to under state law, has not fulfilled a wage judgment, or is in violation of an injunction or court order regarding the payment of wages to its workers.
rules.notes: Failure of AG to give the 30-day notice is not a defense. Denied licenses are subject to B&P 486(a) waiting period. Tool: track outstanding wage judgments/orders as a license-risk flag.

verification.checked_against: 2026 CSLB Law Book (sources/lawbook.txt), PDF pages 262-263 (B&P 7036; added Stats 2025 ch 567, AB 1002, eff. Jan 1, 2026)
verification.correction: The 30-day AG notice, the 60-day intervention window, the good-faith wage-rate exception and the quote are confirmed. The parameter counts_as_discipline_for listed both 7071.8 and 7124.6, but 7036(d)(2) says an order is "disciplinary action within the meaning of Section 7071.8 and legal action within the meaning of Section 7124.6". Split it into disciplinary_action_within_meaning_of and legal_action_within_meaning_of.

rules.title: Government/tribal exemption, but no hiring unlicensed contractors
rules.plain_english: Authorized representatives of the U.S., California, federally recognized tribes acting within tribal jurisdiction, and California cities, counties and districts acting in their official capacity are exempt. But the exemption does not let them contract with an unlicensed contractor for work requiring a license.

exempt_entities: federally recognized tribe or participating tribe acting within tribal jurisdiction
other municipal or political corporation or subdivision of the state
parameters.condition: acting within scope of official capacity

rules.applies_to: Public agencies, tribes and their contractors
rules.verbatim_quote: Nothing in this section authorizes the entity or its authorized representative thereof either to enter into or authorize a contract with an unlicensed contractor for work that is required by this chapter to be performed by a licensed contractor.
rules.notes: See Public Contract Code 6100 (Appendix).

rules.title: Court officers exempt
rules.plain_english: Court officers (e.g., receivers) acting within the scope of their office are exempt from the contractor license law.

parameters.condition: acting within the scope of their office

rules.applies_to: Court-appointed officers
rules.verbatim_quote: This chapter does not apply to officers of a court when they are acting within the scope of their office.
rules.notes: Example 'receivers' is illustrative and not in the text.

rules.title: Public utilities: own-business work exempt
rules.plain_english: Regulated public utilities doing construction, maintenance and development work incidental to their own business are exempt.

parameters.exempt: public utilities operating under state regulation
parameters.scope: construction, maintenance and development work incidental to their own business

rules.applies_to: Public utilities
rules.verbatim_quote: This chapter does not apply to public utilities operating under the regulation of the State Railroad Commission on construction, maintenance and development work incidental to their own business.
rules.notes: Text refers to the historical State Railroad Commission; B&P 7042.5 restates this for the Public Utilities Commission.

rules.title: Gas/heat/electric utilities: limits on licensed work
rules.plain_english: PUC-regulated gas, heat and electrical corporations and their subsidiaries may not do work requiring a contractor's license except: on their own properties; through licensed contractors or PUC-authorized low-income programs; for generation/transmission/distribution (including work past the meter if needed for safety or to avoid outage); work otherwise exempt; or PUC-ordered programs.

parameters.who: gas, heat, or electrical corporations and subsidiaries regulated by the PUC
allowed_conditions_any_of: work on the corporation's properties (owned, leased, easement, or facilities owned/operated for utility purposes)
work performed through contract with licensed contractor(s)
work for low-income citizens under PUC-authorized program

work furthering generation, transmission, or distribution of electricity, gas, or steam; work inside a structure beyond the customer's meter only if necessary to protect public safety or avoid service interruption
work to comply with PUC-ordered or authorized programs consistent with Stats 1983 ch 984

rules.applies_to: Energy utilities; contractors competing in energy efficiency work
rules.verbatim_quote: gas heat, or electrical corporations and their subsidiaries that are regulated as public utilities by the Public Utilities Commission shall not conduct work for which a contractor’s license is required, except under any one or more of the following conditions:
rules.notes: Book's table of contents mislabels this section 'Adoption fees; Deferral, waiver, or reduction'.

rules.title: PUC utilities and cable TV exempt, except street trenching
rules.plain_english: PUC-regulated utilities doing work incidental to their own business, and regulated cable TV companies, are exempt, except that a cable TV company's underground trenching in public streets (other than to connect subscribers) requires a licensed contractor.

exempt: public utilities regulated by PUC, work incidental to own business
cable television corporation activities regulated under PUC 768.5
parameters.not_exempt: underground trenching by cable TV corporation within public streets, other than solely for connecting its distribution system to, or within, subscriber/potential subscriber properties
parameters.cable_tv_corporation_definition: corporation or person that transmits television programs by cable to subscribers for a fee

rules.applies_to: Utilities, cable TV companies, trenching contractors
rules.verbatim_quote: except underground trenching by a cable television corporation within the public streets, other than that necessary solely for the connection of its distribution system to, or within the properties of, subscribers or potential subscribers.

rules.title: Oil and gas well work by owner or lessee exempt
rules.plain_english: Construction, repair or operation incidental to discovering or producing oil or gas, or drilling, testing or abandoning oil/gas wells, is exempt when done by the owner or lessee.

scope: construction, repair or operation incidental to discovering or producing petroleum or gas
drilling, testing, abandoning or other operation of petroleum or gas well

rules.applies_to: Oil and gas owners/lessees
rules.verbatim_quote: This chapter does not apply to any construction, repair or operation incidental to the discovering or producing of petroleum or gas, or the drilling, testing, abandoning or other operation of any petroleum or gas well, when performed by an owner or lessee.
rules.notes: Contractors hired by the owner/lessee are not covered by this exemption on its face.

rules.title: Owner-builder exemption: self-performed, not for sale
rules.plain_english: An owner who builds or improves a structure on their own property is exempt if none of the improvements are intended or offered for sale, and the owner personally does all the work or uses only their own employees paid wages as their sole compensation.

conditions_all: none of the improvements intended or offered for sale
owner personally performs all work, or any other work is by owner's employees with wages as sole compensation

rules.applies_to: Property owners building or improving their own property
rules.verbatim_quote: (A) None of the improvements are intended or offered for sale. (B) The property owner personally performs all of the work or any work not performed by the owner is performed by the owner’s employees with wages as their sole compensation.
rules.notes: Owner using employees takes on employer obligations (payroll, workers' comp) not addressed in this section. See sale presumptions in 7044(b).

rules.title: Owner-builder exemption: owner contracts directly with licensed trades
rules.plain_english: An owner building or improving on their own property is exempt if they contract directly with properly licensed contractors for each trade. For single-family homes, no more than four may be intended or offered for sale in a calendar year, unless the owner hires a general contractor for the construction.

conditions_all: owner directly contracts with licensees duly licensed for the respective trades
parameters.sfr_limit_waived_if: owner contracts with a general contractor for the construction

rules.applies_to: Owner-builders and small developers
rules.verbatim_quote: (B) For projects involving single-family residential structures, no more than four of these structures are intended or offered for sale in a calendar year. This subparagraph shall not apply if the owner contracts with a general contractor for the construction.
rules.notes: Tool check: count SFR structures intended/offered for sale per calendar year; >4 without a GC means owner needs a license.

rules.title: Homeowner improving own principal residence (12-month residency)
rules.plain_english: A homeowner improving their principal residence is exempt if the work is done before sale, they actually lived there for the 12 months before the work was completed, and they have not used this exemption on more than two structures more than once in any three-year period.

conditions_all: homeowner actually resided in residence for 12 months prior to completion of the work
has not used this exemption on more than two structures more than once during any three-year period
parameters.covers: principal place of residence or appurtenances

rules.applies_to: Homeowners improving their primary residence
rules.verbatim_quote: (A) The work is performed prior to sale. (B) The homeowner has actually resided in the residence for the 12 months prior to completion of the work. (C) The homeowner has not availed himself or herself of the exemption in this paragraph on more than two structures more than once during any three-year period.
rules.notes: The 'more than two structures more than once during any three-year period' wording is ambiguous; confirm interpretation before hard-coding.

rules.title: Nonprofit assisting mutual self-help owner-builders exempt
rules.plain_english: A nonprofit corporation helping an owner-builder who participates in a mutual self-help housing program is exempt.

parameters.exempt: nonprofit corporation providing assistance to an owner-builder (HSC 50692(a))

rules.applies_to: Affordable housing nonprofits
rules.verbatim_quote: A nonprofit corporation providing assistance to an owner-builder, as defined in subdivision (a) of Section 50692 of the Health and Safety Code, who is participating in a mutual self-help housing program, as defined in Section 50078 of the Health and Safety Code.

rules.title: Owner-builder sale within 1 year presumed built for sale
rules.plain_english: If an owner-builder sells or offers to sell a structure within one year after completion, the law presumes it was built for sale (the owner can try to rebut this). Selling or offering five or more structures within one year after completion is conclusive proof they were built for sale.

parameters.presumption: structure undertaken for purposes of sale (defeats 7044 exemptions that require no sale intent)

rules.applies_to: Owner-builders selling completed structures
rules.verbatim_quote: proof of the sale or offering for sale of a structure by or for the owner-builder within one year after completion of the structure constitutes a rebuttable presumption affecting the burden of proof that the structure was undertaken for purposes of sale.
rules.notes: Conclusive presumption text: 'Proof of the sale or offering for sale of five or more structures by the owner-builder within one year after completion constitutes a conclusive presumption that the structures were undertaken for purposes of sale.'

rules.title: Injunctions against unlicensed, non-exempt owner-builders
rules.plain_english: Licensed contractors, contractor associations, labor organizations, affected consumers, district attorneys or the Attorney General can sue for an injunction against an owner-builder who is neither licensed nor exempt, without proving irreparable injury. The prevailing party (plaintiff or defendant) gets attorney's fees and costs.

parameters.defendant: owner-builder who is neither licensed nor exempt
parameters.attorney_fees: prevailing party (plaintiff or defendant) recovers attorney's fees and all costs

rules.applies_to: Owner-builders; competing contractors
rules.verbatim_quote: any licensed contractor or association of contractors, labor organization, consumer affected by the violation, district attorney, or the Attorney General shall be entitled to seek injunctive relief prohibiting any violation of this chapter by an owner-builder who is neither licensed nor exempted from licensure under this chapter.
rules.notes: Two-way fee shifting creates risk for plaintiffs who lose.

rules.title: Real estate licensees exempt only within real estate scope
rules.plain_english: Real estate licensees acting within their real estate license are exempt, but neither a real estate licensee nor a property manager may act as a contractor without a CSLB license.

parameters.exempt: real estate licensee acting within course and scope of license (B&P 10000 et seq.)
not_authorized_without_cslb_license: real estate licensee acting as contractor

rules.applies_to: Real estate agents/brokers and property managers
rules.verbatim_quote: However, nothing in this section shall authorize a real estate licensee or a property manager to act in the capacity of a contractor unless licensed by the board.
rules.notes: Property managers arranging and overseeing repairs should check B&P 7026.1(a)(2) consultant rules too.

rules.title: Surety completing a bonded contract is exempt
rules.plain_english: An admitted surety insurer that hires a contractor to complete a contract it bonded (performance or completion bond) is exempt, as long as all actual construction is done by licensed contractors.

parameters.condition_1: surety engages a contractor to complete a contract on which it issued a performance or completion bond
parameters.condition_2: all actual construction work performed by duly licensed contractors

rules.applies_to: Sureties and completion contractors; owners after contractor default
rules.verbatim_quote: This chapter does not apply to an admitted surety insurer whenever that surety insurer engages a contractor to undertake the completion of a contract on which a performance or completion bond was issued by the surety insurer, provided all actual construction work is performed by duly licensed contractors.

rules.title: Finished products not fixed to structure; non-installing suppliers exempt
rules.plain_english: Selling or installing finished products that do not become a fixed part of the structure is exempt, as are suppliers/manufacturers that do not install or contract to install. But installed carpets, mobilehomes and mobilehome accessory structures are not 'finished products', and installing home improvement goods is covered by the license law.

exempt: sale or installation of finished products, materials, or merchandise that do not become a fixed part of the structure
material supplier or manufacturer who does not install or contract for installation

rules.applies_to: Suppliers, manufacturers, retailers offering installation
rules.verbatim_quote: This chapter does not apply to the sale or installation of any finished products, materials, or articles of merchandise that do not become a fixed part of the structure, nor shall it apply to a material supplier or manufacturer furnishing finished products, materials, or articles of merchandise who does not install or contract for the installation of those items.
rules.notes: Second paragraph: 'This chapter shall apply to the installation of home improvement goods, as defined in Section 7151.'

rules.title: Personal property work exempt (not mobilehomes)
rules.plain_english: Work on personal property is exempt, but mobilehomes and mobilehome accessory structures are not treated as personal property for this exemption.

parameters.exempt: construction, alteration, improvement, or repair of personal property

rules.applies_to: Persons working on movable property
rules.verbatim_quote: This chapter does not apply to any construction, alteration, improvement, or repair of personal property. The term “personal property” shall not include mobilehomes or mobilehome accessory structures as defined in Section 7026.2.

rules.title: Minor work exemption: under $1,000 total and no building permit
rules.plain_english: No license is needed for casual, minor work on one project if the total price of all contracts for labor, materials and everything else is under $1,000 and the work does not require a building permit.

parameters.aggregation: all contracts on one undertaking or project
parameters.test: aggregate_price < 1000 AND NOT permit_required AND NOT part_of_larger_operation AND NOT split_to_evade AND NOT advertises_as_contractor AND NOT employs_others

rules.applies_to: Handypersons and owners hiring for small jobs
rules.verbatim_quote: This chapter does not apply to a work or operation on one undertaking or project by one or more contracts if the aggregate contract price for labor, materials, and all other items is less than one thousand dollars ($1,000), that work or operation being considered of casual, minor, or inconsequential nature, and the work or operation does not require a building permit.
rules.effective: January 1, 2025 (Stats 2024 ch 240, AB 2622); further amended effective January 1, 2026 (Stats 2025 ch 67, AB 1170)
rules.notes: Strictly less than $1,000; $1,000.00 exactly requires a license. Previous threshold ($500) is not stated in this text.

rules.title: Minor work exemption: no splitting or parts of larger jobs
rules.plain_english: The under-$1,000 exemption does not apply if the work is part of a larger operation (by the same or a different contractor), or if the job is broken into contracts under $1,000 to evade the law or otherwise.

disqualifiers: work is only part of a larger or major operation, whether by same or different contractor
operation divided into contracts under $1,000 for purpose of evasion or otherwise

rules.applies_to: Unlicensed persons relying on the minor-work exemption; owners hiring them
rules.verbatim_quote: This section does not apply in a case wherein the work of construction is only a part of a larger or major operation, whether undertaken by the same or a different contractor, or in which a division of the operation is made in contracts of amounts less than one thousand dollars ($1,000) for the purpose of evasion of this chapter or otherwise.
rules.notes: Tool check: sum all contracts/invoices with the same person on the same project; flag multiple sub-$1,000 contracts.

rules.title: Minor work exemption lost if you advertise as contractor or employ others
rules.plain_english: The under-$1,000 exemption does not apply to anyone who advertises or uses signs/cards suggesting they are a contractor or qualified to be one, or who employs anyone else to do or help with the work.

disqualifiers: advertises or puts out sign, card or device indicating the person is a contractor or qualified to engage in contracting
employs another person to perform or assist in performing the work

rules.applies_to: Unlicensed handypersons
rules.verbatim_quote: This section does not apply to a person who does either of the following: (1) Advertises or puts out a sign or card or other device that might indicate to the public that the person is a contractor or that the person is qualified to engage in the business of a contractor. (2) Employs another person to perform, or assist in performing, the work or operation.
rules.notes: Compare B&P 7027.2 (unlicensed ads for <$1,000 work allowed only with a 'not licensed' statement).

rules.title: Agricultural, district ditch and rural fire-prevention work exempt
rules.plain_english: Work incidental to building/repairing irrigation and drainage ditches of irrigation or reclamation districts, farming, dairying, agriculture, viticulture, horticulture, livestock or poultry raising, and rural land clearing for fire prevention is exempt, except when done by a licensee. Water well work is not exempt.

exempt_activities: construction/repair of irrigation and drainage ditches of regularly constituted irrigation or reclamation districts
clearing or other work on land in rural districts for fire prevention
parameters.exemption_lost_if: performed by a licensee under the chapter
parameters.not_exempt: water well drilling, digging, boring, constructing, deepening, repairing, reperforating, or abandoning

rules.applies_to: Farmers, ranchers, rural landowners, districts
rules.verbatim_quote: This chapter does not apply to any construction or operation incidental to the construction and repair of irrigation and drainage ditches of regularly constituted irrigation districts, reclamation districts, or to farming, dairying, agriculture, viticulture, horticulture, or stock or poultry raising
rules.notes: Text: '... or clearing or other work upon the land in rural districts for fire prevention purposes, except when performed by a licensee under this chapter.'

rules.title: Mural artists exempt (not painted wall signs)
rules.plain_english: An artist who draws, paints, applies, executes, restores or conserves a mural under an agreement with someone who can legally authorize it does not need a contractor's license. A 'mural' is a unique hand-made work of fine art directly on walls, ceilings or fixtures; painted wall signs are not murals.

parameters.exempt: artist who draws, paints, applies, executes, restores, or conserves a mural
parameters.condition: agreement with a person who could legally authorize the work
parameters.mural_definition: unique work of fine art protected by copyright, trademark, label, or patent, drawn or painted by hand directly onto interior or exterior walls, ceilings, fixtures, or other appurtenances

rules.applies_to: Mural artists; owners commissioning murals
rules.verbatim_quote: This chapter does not apply to an artist who draws, paints, applies, executes, restores, or conserves a mural pursuant to an agreement with a person who could legally authorize the work.
rules.notes: Painted wall signs remain covered (e.g., sign/painting classifications).

rules.title: Architects, engineers, pest control operators, geologists exempt within practice
rules.plain_english: Licensed architects and registered civil/professional engineers acting solely in their professional capacity, licensed structural pest control operators within their license, and licensees under the Geologist and Geophysicist Act within its scope are exempt.
rules.applies_to: Design professionals and pest control operators
rules.verbatim_quote: This chapter does not apply to a licensed architect or a registered civil or professional engineer acting solely in his or her professional capacity or to a licensed structural pest control operator acting within the scope of his or her license or a licensee operating within the scope of the Geologist and Geophysicist Act.
rules.notes: Design-build or construction management beyond professional services may require a CSLB license.

rules.title: Material suppliers who don't install are exempt
rules.plain_english: A person who only furnishes materials or supplies, without fabricating them into or consuming them in the contractor's work, is exempt.

parameters.exempt: person who only furnishes materials or supplies
parameters.condition: does not fabricate them into, or consume them in the performance of, the work

rules.applies_to: Material suppliers
rules.verbatim_quote: This chapter does not apply to any person who only furnishes materials or supplies without fabricating them into, or consuming them in the performance of, the work of the contractor.

rules.title: Wage employees exempt (3-part test)
rules.plain_english: A worker is exempt as an employee only if they are paid wages as their sole compensation, do not customarily run an independent business, and have no right to control how the work is done to determine its final results. This exemption does not apply to home improvement salespersons (Article 10).

conditions_all: does not customarily engage in an independently established business
does not have right to control or discretion as to manner of performance so as to determine final results
parameters.not_applicable_to: Article 10 (B&P 7150 et seq.) home improvement business, e.g., salespersons

rules.applies_to: Contractors classifying workers; owners using workers directly
rules.verbatim_quote: Except as provided in Article 10 (commencing with Section 7150), this chapter does not apply to any person who engages in the activities herein regulated as an employee who receives wages as his or her sole compensation, does not customarily engage in an independently established business, and does not have the right to control or discretion as to the manner of performance
rules.notes: Workers paid by the job/1099 who control the means of work are likely 'contractors' needing a license. Labor Code worker-classification tests are separate.

rules.title: Licensed alarm company operators exempt for alarm work
rules.plain_english: A person holding an alarm company operator's license (B&P 7590 et seq.) is exempt for installing, maintaining, monitoring, selling, altering or servicing alarm systems.

parameters.exempt: holder of alarm company operator's license (B&P Chapter 11.6)
parameters.of: alarm systems as defined in B&P 7590.1

rules.applies_to: Alarm companies
rules.verbatim_quote: This chapter does not apply to any person who performs work in the installation, maintenance, monitoring, selling, alteration, or servicing of alarm systems, as defined in Section 7590.1, and who holds an alarm company operator’s license issued pursuant to Chapter 11.6 (commencing with Section 7590).

rules.title: Registered satellite antenna installers exempt (residential)
rules.plain_english: A person registered under B&P Chapter 20 whose only activity is installing satellite antenna systems on residential structures or property is exempt from the licensing provisions.

parameters.exempt: person registered under B&P Chapter 20 (commencing with 9800)
parameters.condition: activities consist only of installing satellite antenna systems

rules.applies_to: Satellite antenna installers
rules.verbatim_quote: The licensing provisions of this chapter do not apply to any person registered under Chapter 20 (commencing with Section 9800) if that person’s activities consist only of installing satellite antenna systems on residential structures or property.

rules.title: Three branches of contracting (A, B/B-2, C)
rules.plain_english: For licensing classification, contracting is divided into general engineering contracting (A), general building contracting (B), residential remodeling contracting, and specialty contracting (C).
rules.applies_to: All contractors and owners choosing a contractor
rules.verbatim_quote: For the purpose of classification, the contracting business includes any or all of the following branches: (a) General engineering contracting. (b) (1) General building contracting. (2) Residential remodeling contracting. (c) Specialty contracting.
rules.notes: Letter codes A, B, B-2 and C are not printed in this section; residential remodeling is defined in B&P 7057.5 (outside this chunk).

rules.title: General engineering (A) contractor scope
rules.plain_english: A general engineering contractor's main business is fixed works requiring specialized engineering knowledge, such as irrigation, water supply, flood control, harbors, dams, railroads, highways, streets, tunnels, airports, sewers, bridges, pipelines, parks, refineries and plants, power plants, mines, earthmoving, excavating, grading, trenching, paving and related concrete work.

parameters.principal_business: fixed works requiring specialized engineering knowledge and skill
listed_works: levees, river control and reclamation works
sewers and sewage disposal plants and systems
bridges, overpasses, underpasses and similar works
pipelines for petroleum and other liquid or gaseous substances
parks, playgrounds and other recreational works
refineries, chemical plants and similar industrial plants
powerhouses, powerplants and other utility plants and installations
excavating, grading, trenching, paving and surfacing work
cement and concrete works in connection with the above

rules.applies_to: A-licensed contractors; owners of infrastructure projects
rules.verbatim_quote: A general engineering contractor is a contractor whose principal contracting business is in connection with fixed works requiring specialized engineering knowledge and skill, including the following divisions or subjects:
rules.notes: Letter code 'A' not printed in this section.

rules.title: General building (B) contractor: two unrelated trades
rules.plain_english: A general building contractor's main business is structures for sheltering people, animals or property that require at least two unrelated building trades or crafts, or supervising all or part of such work. Someone who only supplies materials is not a general building contractor.

parameters.structure_purpose: support, shelter, and enclosure of persons, animals, chattels, or movable property
parameters.includes: doing or superintending the whole or any part thereof
parameters.excludes: material suppliers under B&P 7045 who do not fabricate or consume materials in the work

rules.applies_to: B-licensed contractors and owners hiring GCs
rules.verbatim_quote: a general building contractor is a contractor whose principal contracting business is in connection with any structure built, being built, or to be built, for the support, shelter, and enclosure of persons, animals, chattels, or movable property of any kind, requiring in its construction the use of at least two unrelated building trades or crafts
rules.notes: Section 7057 appears on PDF page 271, just past the nominal end of this chunk.

rules.title: B contractor prime/sub limits: two unrelated trades besides framing/carpentry
rules.plain_english: A B contractor may take any framing or carpentry job. For other trades, a B may take a prime contract only if the job requires at least two unrelated trades other than framing/carpentry, or the B holds the specialty license, or subcontracts that work to a properly licensed contractor. A B may take a subcontract for other trades only if it requires two unrelated trades other than framing/carpentry, or the B holds the specialty license. Framing/carpentry never counts toward the two trades.

prime_contract_other_trades_allowed_if_a: requires >= 2 unrelated building trades or crafts other than framing or carpentry
B holds the appropriate specialty classification
B subcontracts with an appropriately licensed contractor to perform the work
subcontract_other_trades_allowed_if_any: requires >= 2 unrelated trades or crafts other than framing or carpentry
B holds the appropriate specialty classification

rules.applies_to: B general building contractors; owners and GCs awarding work to B contractors
rules.verbatim_quote: a general building contractor shall not take a prime contract for any project involving trades other than framing or carpentry unless the prime contract requires at least two unrelated building trades or crafts other than framing or carpentry, or unless the general building contractor holds the appropriate license classification or subcontracts with an appropriately licensed contractor
rules.notes: Tool check: count distinct unrelated trades in scope excluding framing/carpentry; if < 2, B needs matching C classification (prime: or a licensed sub; subcontract: own classification only).

rules.title: B contractor: fire protection and well drilling need license or sub
rules.plain_english: A B general building contractor may not contract for a project that includes a fire protection system or C-57 well drilling unless it holds that classification or subcontracts the work to a properly licensed contractor.

allowed_if_any: B subcontracts with the appropriately licensed contractor

rules.applies_to: B general building contractors
rules.verbatim_quote: A general building contractor shall not contract for any project that includes a fire protection system as provided for in Section 7026.12 or 7026.13, or the “C-57” Well Drilling classification as provided for in Section 13750.5 of the Water Code, unless the general building contractor holds the appropriate license classification, or subcontracts with the appropriately licensed contractor.
rules.notes: Applies even when the project otherwise meets the two-unrelated-trades test.
